'''Eleonora Di Nezza''' is an Italian mathematician, a [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] researcher at the [[Centre de mathématiques Laurent-Schwartz]] and a professor of mathematics at [[Ecole Polytechnique]],<ref>[https://www.polytechnique.edu/en/content/cnrs-bronze-medal-eleonora-di-nezza CNRS bronze medal for Eleonora Di Nezza] – Ecole Polytechnique</ref> in [[Palaiseau]], [[France]]. Her research is at the intersection of various branches of mathematics<ref>[http://maddmaths.simai.eu/persone/11768/ Eleonora Di Nezza: geometria complessa… e yoga] – MaddMAths</ref> including complex and differential geometry,<ref>[https://france.math.cnrs.fr/portraits/#popup551 Eleonora Di Nezza] – Math in France</ref> and focuses on [[Kähler manifold|Kähler geometry]].<ref>[https://www.ihes.fr/entretien-avec-eleonora-di-nezza/ Entretien avec Eleonora Di Nezza] – IHÉS</ref>

==Education and career ==
Di Nezza earned her master's degree in mathematics from the [[Sapienza University of Rome]],<ref>[https://perso.pages.math.cnrs.fr/users/eleonora.di-nezza/media/CVDiNezza.pdf CV Eleonora Di Nezza] – CNRS</ref> and did her doctoral research between the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]] and [[Toulouse III - Paul Sabatier University|Paul Sabatier University]] in [[Toulouse]], [[France]], during which reunified results on fractional [[Sobolev space|Sobolev spaces]] in collaboration with Giampiero Palatucci and Enrico Valdinoci.<ref>[http://maddmaths.simai.eu/persone/11768/ Eleonora Di Nezza: geometria complessa… e yoga] – MaddMAths</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/j.bulsci.2011.12.004|title=Hitchhikerʼs guide to the fractional Sobolev spaces|year=2012|last1=Di Nezza|first1=Eleonora|last2=Palatucci|first2=Giampiero|last3=Valdinoci|first3=Enrico|journal=Bulletin des Sciences Mathématiques|volume=136|issue=5|pages=521–573|s2cid=55443959|doi-access=free|arxiv=1104.4345}}</ref> Her dissertation was on the
Geometry of complex Monge-Ampère equations on compact Kähler manifolds.<ref>"[https://auf.hal.science/tel-01429436/ Geometry of complex Monge-Ampère equations on compact Kähler manifolds]," PhD dissertation, Eleonora Di Nezza – HAL</ref>

After receiving her PhD, she became a postdoctoral fellow at [[Imperial College]], in [[London]], [[UK]] under a [[Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions|Marie Curie Fellowship]], during which she joined the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]], United States. In 2017 she moved to France to join the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques|Institute of Advanced Scientific Studies]] before becoming a lecturer at [[Sorbonne University]] and a professor of mathematics at [[Ecole Polytechnique]].

==Recognition==
She was awarded the [[CNRS Bronze Medal]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.polytechnique.edu/en/content/cnrs-bronze-medal-eleonora-di-nezza|title = École Polytechnique - Accueil site de l'Ecole Polytechnique}}</ref><ref>[https://www.insmi.cnrs.fr/fr/cnrsinfo/les-travaux-deleonora-di-nezza-medaille-de-bronze-2021 Les travaux d’Eleonora Di Nezza, médaille de bronze 2021] – CNRS</ref> She was the 2023 recipient of the Prix Reine-Elizabeth from the Pierre Le Conte Foundation of the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=leconte>{{cite web|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Laureats/laureats-2023-des-prix-thematiques.html|title=Lauréats 2023 des prix thématiques |language=fr|publisher=French Academy of Sciences|access-date=2024-08-09}}</ref>

In 2023 she was named as a junior member to the [[Institut Universitaire de France]].<ref name=leconte/>
